prerequisites:
Electrical circuits: basic electrical bipoles, Kirchhoff
				’s laws, electrical circuits analysis, use of operational amplifiers in linear networks

learning_outcomes.text: understand the operation of elementary electronic devices (diodes and MOSFETs)
analyze the operation of simple electronic circuits containing diodes, MOSFETs, and operational amplifiers
understand the working principles of a digital electronic circuit
analyse the processing algorithm performed by a combinatorial network
understand the processing algorithm performed by a sequential network
understand the architecture of a microprocessor-based system
independently use the materials and instrumentation available in the laboratory to assemble simple analog and digital electronic circuits and perform measurements on them

syllabus_topics: Diodes: characteristics and examples of circuit applications. Photodiodes, photovoltaic cells, and LEDs.
MOSFET transistors: characteristics and applications in analog and digital circuits.
Signal processing circuits with operational amplifiers.
Op Amp with positive feedback: waveform generators.

Combinatorial networks. Half adder and full adder. Decoder. Multiplexer. Asynchronous sequential networks. SR latch. Synchronous sequential networks. Flip-flops. Performance of digital electric circuits. Digital electronic technology evolution. Microprocessor-based systems. Von Neuman architecture and Harvard architecture. CPU, memory and I/O unit main features. Functional units communication: handshaking. System bus performance. CPU microarchitecture. Instruction cycle. CPU registers and data path. Instruction set architecture. CISC and RISC instructions. Memory hierarchy. I/O activities: programmed, interrupt, DMA. Hardware accelerators for machine learning.
Assembly and analysis of simple analog and digital circuits.
Use of basic electronic instrumentation: power supplies, function generators, multimeters, oscilloscopes.

assessment_methods.method: Written test - Part 1: two short exercises
Written test - Part 1: one open question
Written test - Part 2: two open questions
Additional question on laboratory material (for non-attendees)

assessment_rules: The assessment is through a single written test. To pass the written test, a score of at least 18/30 is required, with at least 6 points in each part of the course. If the written test score is below 18/30, the exam is not passed and must be repeated. Attending at least 75% of laboratory activities and submitting a short report can add up to 3 points to the final grade. Alternatively, students unable to attend labs will have an additional question on the material in the written exam, worth up to 3 points. A short oral exam, if requested, can contribute up to +/- 2 points to the final grade. Two mid-term written tests are scheduled, which can replace the final written exam if passed.
